  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS
Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social
distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the Assembly
Bill 361, please note that members of the public will only be allowed
to observe and address the Planning Commission of December 1, 2021
at 7:00 P.M. by telephone, video and other means, as follows:

Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members
of the public may listen and make oral public comments
telephonically by dialing:

  Dial-in:  1-888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694
  Access Code:  7194435# wait 2 seconds and press # again

Please observe the following tips when phoning in:
   When you call-in, the operator will provide further
  instructions on how you can make public comments via phone.
   If you are calling from a cell phone, please call from an area
  with good reception.
   If you are watching the meeting on Facebook or Channel 35 while
  also accessing the phone line, it is requested that you mute the
  sound of your video feed as it is offset by 3 seconds from the
  phone transmission. Additionally, when you are making public
  comments on the phone line you will be inaudible due to feedback.

Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:
   On Spectrum Cable Local Channel 35 with audio and limited video.
  Please check with your cable provider for details.
   Live on-line through Facebook Live, with audio and limited
  video, at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

Written Public Comments: Members of the public can submit comments
for consideration by the Planning Commission by sending them to Mindy
Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager at mwilcox@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Planning Commission prior
to consideration of the agenda, comments must be received prior to
12:00 P.M. on December 1, 2021, the day of the meeting. Correspondence
should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received
after 12:00 P.M. and prior to close of the public hearing will be
made part of the official public record of the meeting.

Accessibility: If you will require special accommodations due to a
disability, please contact the Planning Division Office at (310) 412-
5230, One Manchester Boulevard, 4th Floor, Inglewood, California
90301.  All requests for accommodations must be received 48 hours

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, May 6, 2020 in the Council
Chambers on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge of

at 7:10 p.m., to allow the listening and watching audience an
opportunity to dial in.

(5) PUBLIC HEARING:

5A. GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT 2020-001 (GPA-2020-001).
A public hearing to reconsider General Plan Amendment 2020-001
(GPA 2020-001) to adopt an Environmental Justice Element to the
General Plan.
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
May 6, 2020

Mr. Fred Jackson, Senior Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice stated no questions.

Commissioner Patrick stated she had a couple of comments for staff–
 In staff’s discussion she believes that the Environmental
  Justice Element should be made a prime term in staff’s report
  and states this is an very good report, but feels that it should
  be addressed even in the staff report as a prime term of the
  report, in that the purpose of Environmental Justice Element is
  to discuss in depth disadvantaged communities which is not
  generally discussed in the General Plan, as this is why the
  Environmental Justice Element would differ from the General Plan
  because it does speak to disadvantaged communities and she feels
  this should be stated in the document, also on page two, staff
  stated that the state of California is mentioned with all races,
  cultures and income levels and she feels that national origin
  should be mentioned as well.

Commissioner Rice has a statement to make to staff –
 With regards to the disadvantaged community position which the
  City finds itself in, is there anything that the City can do to
  help with moving the City forward, with regards to some overview
  information from the past that the Planning Commission can be
  given which will help us in deciding upon what our City will be
  used for – such as our live Fire training center that is being
  performed here in Inglewood from the various other cities nearby
  such as Santa Monica, El Segundo, Hawthorne, Culver City, where
  they have shut down their live fire training centers, and we
  could possibly see what was approved in the past so that we can
  either lessen the hours allowed for the live burnings from the
  other cities or have the training only for the local stations
  from this city, and have all of the other cities go out to the
  valley areas such as Tehachapi, or somewhere in the open Valley
  areas, away from polluting our air system here in Inglewood?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that we can reach out to the Air Quality
  District and find out what restrictions that they are required
  to operate under and determine if they are operating outside
  of that.

  Is there a way that this planning commission could receive a
  copy of the guidelines and also forward a copy to Code
  Enforcement if they are indeed working outside of their
  permitted restrictions so that they can address the issue?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated yes, we can.

tenant space within an existing three-story 16,350 square-foot

Ms. Taylor Kay, Assistant Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs Larry asked the Planning Commission if there were
any questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff several questions–
 About the elevation;
   Ms. Kay answered it is not a requirement.
 Will the canopy will be reviewed by public works, but not the
  planning commission?
   Ms. Kay stated that there will be a design review process with
  the planning division and an additional process from the public
  works department.
 He stated he would like to see what the canopy would look like?
   Ms. Kay stated the applicant did submit a rendering with their
  partial elevation that was submitted already.

Commissioner Trejo stated she had questions for staff –
 Although this is just a design review, in staff’s report, it
  mentions that the applicant will use the second and third floors
  for co-working spaces, what does this mean?
   Ms. Kay stated the concept the applicant is proposing, is for
  short term or long term office space rentals on the second and
  third floor in an open office area.
 So this is not just for the coffee shop correct?
   Ms. Kay stated that the coffee shop will be on the first floor
  and the applicant will be doing tenant improvements there where
  the design review is only for the facade improvements to the
  first floor coffee shop. The second and third floors will be
  for rentals.
 So does this mean the applicant does not have to come before the
  planning commission for any of the tenant improvements or use on
  the second and third floors?
   Ms. Kay stated no, that is a by-right use.
 Commissioner Trejo also asked about the signage for both the coffee
  shop and the co-working office space, will it be subject to signage
  review or site plan review?
   Ms. Kay stated that a mural is subject to a design review under
  the municipal code sign regulations, and any other type of
  signage typically goes through a sign adjustment or a sign
  permit, since it is a multi-tenant building it will also need
  a master sign program, but not to say it will have to come back
  to the planning commission, unless it goes through a sign
  adjustment and it is appealed.
 Has there been any work started on the project façade yet?
   Ms. Kay stated that there has been some tenant improvements
  along with the façade.

Commissioner Rice asked staff –
 Since you mentioned the applicant will be renting out the second

A non-public hearing to consider an application by Sandy Sigal,
representing NewMark Merrill Companies, for Design Review No.
2020-006 (DR-2020-006) to allow a 936 square-foot mural on the
exterior of a one-story commercial building that is part of an
existing shopping center on an approximately 17-acre, C-2(General
Commercial) zoned property at 2876 West Imperial Highway.

Mr. Art Salazar, Planner made the staff presentation.
Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick made a statement:
 The local news is noticing Inglewood & Imperial Highway in a
  very positive light, this mural will add to that positive
  acknowledgement, especially since there is a signal light there,
  everyone will be able to see it.

Commissioner Rice made a statement:
 There is another Mural on El Segundo that is very similar to
  this one, he stated he likes the concept and the mural idea and
  thanks for picking Inglewood for the next mural.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff:

  Likes the concept of this mural, the colors are beautiful, the
  quote is great, but the question she has is will there be
  lighting applied so that the art can be appreciated in the
  evening?
   Mr. Salazar stated that at the present time the applicant
  does not propose any lighting at the site.
  Will the mural reach all the way to the ground?
   Mr. Salazar stated, yes.
  Has a concern if the area is dark, and there is the space for
  tagging and/or graffiti, it can damage the mural. This is a
  concern and will ask the applicant.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams made a comment:
 The mural is beautiful, and murals with positive messages
  uplifts the community. Generally murals discourages graffiti,
  because the community feels that pride in the mural, so very
  excited and glad for this mural.

Chairman Springs stated:
 He also likes the mural and finds it very appealing. But that
  he too has the same concern that was mentioned by Commissioner
  Trejo regarding no lighting on that side of the building, and
  asks staff if the applicant is not willing to put any additional
  lighting on that side of the building?
   Mr. Salazar stated that the shopping center has plenty of
  lighting in the front of the buildings and parking lot light
  fixtures, the building also has light fixtures in the front,
  but the artist has not made any proposals to date to add any
  lighting on that side of the building for the mural.

Chairman Springs asked Commission Rice –
 If the mural that he saw in Gardena, was it only during the
  daytime or did he happen to see it in the evening and if so was
  it well lit?

   Commissioner Rice stated that he has seen it both in the day
  and evening times and it is very well lit as it is in a
  shopping area, but that there is a light directly fixed on
  the mural as well, there in Gardena.

Chairman Springs asked if the applicant was on the AT&T phone line
and in attendance via teleconference.

call line and addressed the Planning Commission.

of the areas to spotlight their work in the community, and it tends
to discourage any graffiti out of respect for the artist’s work.

Chairman Springs asked the  Planning  Commission  if  they  had
questions for the applicant.

Commissioner Patrick asked the applicant;
 You mentioned that your company approaches local artists, do
  you plan on doing any other murals here in the City of Inglewood
  anytime soon?
    Ms. Praug stated that at the present the only site that is
  managed in Inglewood is the Crenshaw/Imperial Plaza and they
  are planning on doing some more murals on a smaller scale in
  the plaza area, calling them art moments.
Commissioner Rice stated –
 Loves the mural and the concept, thank you very much.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant;
 Beautiful mural and wants to make sure it stays that way. Knows
  that there are such beautiful murals in the East Los Angeles
  area and over time, they get tagged or hit with graffiti. Do
  you think that with it reaching parking lot level that kids will
  not come by and tag it?
    Ms. Praug stated that once the mural is finished, we will put
  an anti-graffiti coating over it, along with 24 hour security
  on the site. We feel that the area will be covered. But should
  there be any problems with a tagging and the mural is damaged,
  since the artist is a local one, it makes it easy for us to
  have them re-do the mural. It will be well maintained. If
  there are any tags or graffiti even in the parking lot areas,
  they are always cleared away within 12 hours.
